summary: This note is an excerpt from a fiction work titled 'Book 1 — part 105.' The narrator and a companion share a dinner, and she offers him a bite of a very spicy dish; he takes a large bite and is overwhelmed by the heat. She explains the Scoville scale, claims extreme capsaicin brings endorphin highs, and they tease each other about their hobbies. They then walk toward Dolores Park, where the narrator notices their height difference and a growing crowd humming with energy.
one_line: A narrator's painful encounter with an extremely spicy dish, and his walk with a companion toward a bustling Dolores Park.
key_facts: The narrator says he likes spicy food and usually orders curries with four chilies at Pakistani restaurants.
The narrator took a big bite of the companion's food and described the heat as far worse than horseradish or wasabi.
The companion handed the narrator her horchata, which he used to ease the burning.
The companion explains the Scoville scale used by 'chili-fanciers' to rate pepper heat.
Pure capsaicin is about 15 million Scovilles, Tabasco is about 50,000, and pepper spray is about three million.
The dish the narrator ate is rated at about 200,000 Scovilles, described as about as hot as a mild Scotch Bonnet Pepper.
The companion says she worked up to this level of heat in about a year.
The companion claims extremely hot peppers can reach a million Scovilles, twenty times hotter than Tabasco, and that the resulting endorphins make it a better 'body-stone than hash.'
The companion warns of a 'ferocious ring of fire' when going to the bathroom after eating very hot food.
The narrator calls the companion insane, and she replies that his hobby is building and smashing laptops.
The companion offers the narrator a mister, and he declines with 'Pass.'
The couple leaves the restaurant and heads for Dolores park, with her arm around his waist and his arm around her shoulders.
The narrator notes that the companion is just the right height for his arm around her shoulders, which is new to him because he has never been tall and past girlfriends were his height.
As they turn the corner on 20th Street toward Dolores, they feel a buzz like the hum of a million bees from the crowd streaming toward the park.
